summary.one_liner: fman is a dual-pane file manager for Mac, Windows and Linux that adds fast directory jumping and a plugin system.
use_cases: jump quickly to frequently used folders
manage files side by side in two panes
replace Finder with a dual-pane file manager
extend file manager behavior with plugins
browse files across Mac, Windows and Linux
summary.what_it_does: fman is a dual-pane file manager available for Mac, Windows and Linux. Its "GoTo" feature, opened with ⌘P, lets users jump to a directory by name, and it remembers which folders are visited most often and suggests them first. The page lists example shortcuts such as ~/Downloads, ~/Desktop, ~/Dropbox and /Volumes. It has a plugin system where users can install plugins made by others or write and share their own. The listing describes it as the first dual-pane file manager to integrate features from Sublime Text.
notable: ⌘P GoTo jumps to directories and ranks frequently visited folders first
Sublime Text-style features integrated into a dual-pane file manager
Extensible through a plugin system that supports community-made plugins
caveats: Pricing is not stated on the page text provided
Page text is brief and mostly promotional; specifics beyond navigation and plugins are not described
